newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front will not back Congress, BJP.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front will not back Congress, BJP.

text.p: India's ousted United Front coalition said on Saturday that it would not support efforts by either the Congress party or the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to form a new government.

United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters after a meeting of the coalition's decision-making Steering Committee that the alliance had not considered asking caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda to step down as United Front leader.
"There is no question of supporting the BJP or Congress in forming a government," Reddy said.

"The question of change of leadership does not arise, as the proposal has not been mooted by anyone in the Steering Committee," he said, adding that United Front leaders would hold another meeting at the prime minister's official residence at 8 p.m. (1430 GMT) on Saturday.
Earlier on Saturday, Congress party president Sitaram Kesri said he expected talks between his party and the United Front on the formation of a new government would take place during the day.
Reddy said informal talks with Congress were underway.
